title: Weight typo 1710 instead of 171 is saved with no clamp, warning, or visible flag
steps: Start Session on a Bench Press workout → type '1710' into the Set 1 weight field (aria-label 'Set 1 weight in lbs') meaning to type '171' → type reps '8' → mark the set complete → Finish → Log Workout.
expected: Per judge rules, weird input should not silently produce nonsense downstream (e1RM/progression baseline). The UI should reject/clamp before the set can be marked complete, or at minimum visibly flag it before saving.
actual: 1710 lb saved verbatim to workout_logs with zero clamp, zero warning, zero visible flag at any point (before or after Finish). Confirmed via live run: workout_logs row exercises[0].sets[0].weight === 1710.
why: Re-ran: 1710 lb saved verbatim (workout_logs sets[0].weight=1710), no warning. The code INTENDS to catch this slip (comment at ExerciseCard.jsx:624-628: "a fat-fingered extra digit ... becomes the e1RM, the PR, and the progression baseline") but relies on the HTML max="2000" attribute, which a controlled number input outside form validation never enforces: onChange (line 612) stores any finite value, so even 2255 or 9999 saves. The documented guard is inert; 1710 is also under the cap anyway. Real phone behaves the same (no browser enforces max on typing).
rootCause: src/components/workouts/ExerciseCard.jsx:612 (onChange stores any finite weight) + :629 (max="2000" is decorative, never enforced)
fixHint: Smallest safe fix: when a set is marked complete (handleSetCompleted) and its weight exceeds max(2000) or is >2x the exercise lastPerformance.lastWeight, show an inline "Did you mean X?" / confirm before completing; also clamp/refuse >2000 in onChange so the documented cap is real. The 2x-of-last ratio is a UI threshold (mark tunable), not engine semantics. Engine-side outlier rejection (PERF_DEV_CLAMP in compute_athlete_state.py) is out of scope.

title: Double-tap Finish confirm creates a duplicate workout_schedules row (workout_logs itself stays deduped)
steps: Start Session, complete 1 set, tap Finish → 'Finish Workout' dialog → fire two near-simultaneous native .click() calls on the 'Log Workout' button (bypassing React's disabled-state re-check, simulating a real double-tap race).
expected: Exactly one workout_logs row AND the WorkoutSchedule check-or-create for today stays consistent (one schedule row) — no duplicate rows of any kind.
actual: workout_logs correctly ends up with exactly 1 row: the second insert hits the workout_logs_no_exact_dupes UNIQUE constraint (23505), which the mutation's onError handler correctly treats as success (toast 'Workout already logged.', no error surfaced to the athlete) — this backstop works as designed. BUT workout_schedules ends up with 2 rows for the same workout_id/date: both concurrent mutationFn calls read `existing.length === 0` (schedule not yet created by either) before either write lands, so both create a new WorkoutSchedule row instead of one updating the other's. Confirmed via testDb cleanup count: workout_schedules=2 after a single logical Finish.
evidence: console: 'DB create error on workout_logs: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "workout_logs_no_exact_dupes"' (expected/handled); DB: workout_schedules count=2 for one workout_id after cleanup query, workout_logs count=1 (correct)
suspectFile: src/pages/WorkoutDetail.jsx:800-830 (WorkoutSchedule filter-then-create race, not atomic against the concurrent mutation call)
why: Only reproduces with two btn.click() calls in the same JS task (before React/TanStack flush isPending). Re-ran with a realistic 40ms gap between taps (a fast human double-tap is ~80-150ms): the second tap found the button already disabled (disabled={isPending||isSuccess} at WorkoutDetail.jsx:1670), 1 workout_logs row, 1 workout_schedules row, no errors. Harness artifact, not reachable by a thumb. (Also note: parallel runs of r1-01/02 flaked with Finish disabled; sequential runs were clean.)
rootCause: src/pages/WorkoutDetail.jsx:1670-1671 (guard is state-based, only bypassable within one task)
fixHint: None needed. If ever wanted: a useRef in-flight guard in the onClick before mutate().

title: Deleting a completed set has zero undo affordance anywhere in the flow
steps: Complete set 1 (100x10) and set 2 (105x8) on one exercise, then tap the remove-set control on set 2 (the completed one, deleted by mistake instead of an empty set 3). Observe for any undo affordance (toast action, etc.) before/after the delete, then Finish.
expected: Judge rule: mistakes can be undone (deleted set...). removeSet may legitimately have no built-in undo, but SOME recovery path (toast with Undo, confirmation step) should exist somewhere in the flow.
actual: Confirmed zero undo affordance anywhere — no confirmation dialog before delete, no toast, no Undo action. The remaining set correctly renumbers to set 2 and Finish/save completes without crash or data corruption (set numbering and totals are correct). Note: the surviving (previously-untouched) set's weight/reps fields showed non-null autofill values (e.g. weight 252.5, reps 8) after the delete — this was investigated and is the app's existing 'last performance' autofill seeding from the athlete's Bench Press history (same value appeared in isolated pre-delete debug runs too), NOT data bleeding over from the deleted set. Flagging only the confirmed no-undo gap; the autofill-looks-like-bleed appearance is worth a second look by verify since it reads confusingly (autofill visually resembling residue from the just-deleted set could itself mislead a real athlete into thinking their delete didn't fully take).
evidence: screenshots ui-audit/overnight/shots/r1-03-before-delete.png, r1-03-after-delete.png; DB: workout_logs exercises[0].sets shows correct renumbering, no crash, problems=0
why: Re-ran: tapping the X on a completed set deletes it and its data instantly, no confirm, no toast, no Undo. The X (ExerciseCard.jsx:690-699) sits in the column directly beside the completion check, i.e. exactly where a sweaty-thumb miss lands, and the judge rule names "deleted set" explicitly. Renumbering/save are otherwise correct. The 252.5 value in the surviving set is last-performance autofill (not bleed from the deleted set) and is not a bug.
rootCause: src/hooks/useWorkoutExercises.js:44-59 (removeSet discards the set with no recovery) called from src/components/workouts/ExerciseCard.jsx:693
fixHint: In WorkoutDetail, wrap removeSet: capture the removed set + index, call removeSet, then toast("Set N removed", { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => reinsert at index and renumber } }). Needs a small insertSet(exerciseIndex, setIndex, set) in useWorkoutExercises. Autosave will persist the restore. No engine impact.

title: Offline logging + reconnect saves correctly, but auto-save retries spam the console with no visible backoff
steps: Start session online, context.setOffline(true), complete 2 sets while offline, wait, setOffline(false), dispatch an 'online' event, wait for flush, then Finish.
expected: No error dialog blocks logging while offline; once back online, the pending write flushes automatically; Finish saves the real (155/6, 155/5) data.
actual: End state is correct: no error dialog shown to the athlete, workout_sessions row matches what was logged offline after the flush, and the final workout_logs row has the right 2 completed sets. However, while offline the auto-save effect fired 13 failed write attempts in ~2 seconds (each logging 'Failed to load resource: WebKit encountered an internal error' + 'Error saving workout session progress: TypeError: Load failed' to the console) with no visible backoff/debounce between attempts — harmless to data here, but console/HTTP errors are explicitly in-scope per the runbook goal and this is a real, reproducible pattern that would spam a real phone's battery/network on a longer offline stretch at the gym.
evidence: console: 13x repeated 'Error saving workout session progress' during the offline window; DB: final workout_sessions/workout_logs both correct
suspectFile: src/hooks/useWorkoutSession.js:39-70 (saveProgress / online retry, no backoff seen between failed attempts)
why: Re-ran: end state correct (flush on online, final log right). The "13 attempts" are not a retry loop: the auto-save effect (WorkoutDetail.jsx:365-370) fires once per state change, i.e. once per keystroke/checkbox while offline, and each offline fetch fails instantly (no network, no battery cost). Nothing retries on a timer; the only retry is flushPending on the online event (useWorkoutSession.js:42-72). Sets are mirrored locally first (saveDraft) and saveFailed shows a header marker. Console noise is invisible to the athlete and breaks no judge rule.
fixHint: Optional polish only: skip the network write when navigator.onLine is false and just mark pending. Not a bug.

title: Confirmed: manual Finish and auto-finish stamp different log_date for the same midnight-crossing workout
steps: page.clock set to 23:50 America/Denver on day D, Start Session, complete 2 sets, advance clock to 00:10 on D+1, manually tap Finish → Log Workout.
expected: Documented ambiguity, not necessarily a bug on its own — but the map's suspected inconsistency between the manual-finish and auto-finish paths for the same physical event needed confirming.
actual: Confirmed: manual Finish stamped log_date = D+1 (2026-09-21), i.e. 'today' at the moment of Finish. The auto-finish path for the identical physical scenario (session goes silent instead) stamps log_date = D (session-start day) via localDateOf in buildWorkoutLogFromSession.js — a real, confirmed inconsistency: the same physical workout logs to a different calendar day depending only on which code path happens to close it. Flagging for Nolan's call on which is 'right' (already in wishes.json), not auto-fixing per runbook scope (spec/behavior change).
evidence: DB: workout_logs.log_date=2026-09-21 for a session started 2026-09-20T23:50 Denver; screenshot ui-audit/overnight/shots/r1-08-after-finish.png
suspectFile: src/pages/WorkoutDetail.jsx:770 (getTodayString at Finish time) vs src/lib/buildWorkoutLogFromSession.js (localDateOf at session-start time)
why: Re-ran: session started 23:50 Denver, manual Finish at 00:10 logs log_date = next day (getTodayString at Finish), while the auto-finish path deliberately files under the session start date (buildWorkoutLogFromSession.js:12-13,44, documented: "a forgotten Tuesday workout is filed under Tuesday"). Inconsistency is real, but which day a midnight-crossing workout belongs to is a product/data-semantics call (affects day attribution for engine volume/recovery), not a crash or loss.
rootCause: src/pages/WorkoutDetail.jsx:770 (log_date = getTodayString at Finish) vs src/lib/buildWorkoutLogFromSession.js:44 (localDateOf(startedAt))
fixHint: If Nolan picks session-start day: in saveWorkoutLogMutation use localDateOf(startTime, profile.timezone) instead of getTodayString (same in QuickWorkout.jsx:353). Touches log-date semantics feeding the engine -> Nolan's call.

title: A second identical real workout is silently discarded with a false 'already logged' success toast
steps: Log a workout (same exercises, same weights/reps, same completed-set pattern) through the real app flow twice in a row against the same workout template — e.g. finish a session, then start a fresh session on the same workout and log it identically again.
expected: Two genuinely separate logged sessions should both be saved (or, if the app intends to treat exact-duplicate payloads as a mistaken double-submit, the athlete should be told their second session's data was not saved, not congratulated with a success message).
actual: Confirmed via two real app-driven runs: workout_logs ends with exactly 1 row after both runs (run1Toast=['Workout logged successfully!'], run2Toast=['Workout already logged.']). The second run's insert hits the workout_logs_no_exact_dupes UNIQUE index (md5 of the serialized exercises JSON, same created_by/log_date), and the mutation's onError handler treats Postgres 23505 as unconditional success — a real second workout the athlete just performed and entered is silently thrown away with a toast that reads as good news.
evidence: DB: workout_logs rows=1 after 2 real logged sessions; console/toast text captured in script output (run1Toast/run2Toast)
why: Reproduces (2 identical sessions same day -> 1 row, second toast "Workout already logged."). But this is the deliberate dedupe design: UNIQUE (created_by, log_date, md5(exercises)) is documented in supabase/migrations/20260910000000_workout_logs_no_exact_dupes.sql as the double-submit backstop, and buildWorkoutLogFromSession.js:101-110 explicitly defines "same work" as the duplicate signature. A byte-identical second session (same exercises, same weights, reps, completion pattern, same day) is extremely unlikely for Nolan; not a bet-on-his-phone data-loss. Attacker over-rated severity. Worth Nolan's call on whether same-day identical work should ever be a second row.
fixHint: Cheapest honest option: if the in-app session id differs from the one that wrote the existing log, change the toast to say this matched a workout already logged today and nothing new was saved. A real fix (include session_id in the dedupe key) needs a schema migration on hosted -> proposal.

title: Exercise-swap 'Enter exercise name' combobox field is covered by the on-screen keyboard; multi-swap progression-transfer race remains unconfirmed
steps: Mid-session (program-sourced workout), open an exercise's menu → Replace exercise → type a new exercise name into the 'Enter exercise name…' combobox.
expected: The field being typed into should stay visible above the on-screen keyboard (per judge/iOS-layer rules, a focused input should never be hidden by the keyboard or pushed under the status bar).
actual: Confirmed via drive.mjs's report(): warning field-hidden-by-keyboard on input[placeholder="Enter exercise name…"], path /workout-detail — 'Focused field is covered by the keyboard or pushed under the status bar.' A single swap otherwise behaves correctly: program_enrollments.progression_state correctly transfers the old exercise's key to the new name (OVN-r1-10 Ex1 -> OVN-r1-10 Swap1) with the old key removed, and the in-app swap note is visible. The original hypothesis for this case — that 4 exercises swapped in quick succession could each read a stale progression_state closure and clobber each other's transferProgressionState write (WorkoutDetail.jsx:1027-1035, async ProgramEnrollment.update not awaited) — could NOT be confirmed or ruled out: automating 4 rapid back-to-back swaps was unreliable because this same keyboard-occlusion issue intermittently covers the next exercise card's menu button after a swap closes, causing the driver to lose track of on-screen elements. This is recorded as inconclusive for the race hypothesis, with the keyboard-occlusion bug itself confirmed as a real, separate finding.
repro: ui-audit/overnight/areas/train-logger/scripts/r1-10.mjs (4-swap race attempt, does not reliably complete); single-swap confirmation reproduced ad hoc, see evidence
evidence: report() warning: {"code":"field-hidden-by-keyboard","msg":"Focused field is covered by the keyboard or pushed under the status bar","where":"input[type=\"text\"][placeholder=\"Enter exercise name\u2026\"]","path":"/workout-detail"}; DB: progression_state keys after single swap = ["OVN-r1-10 Ex2","OVN-r1-10 Ex3","OVN-r1-10 Ex4","OVN-r1-10 Swap1"] (transferred=true, origGone=true); screenshot ui-audit/overnight/shots/r1-10-single-after-swap.png
suspectFile: src/components/workouts/ExerciseCard.jsx:785-835 (Replace dialog / Combobox layout); src/pages/WorkoutDetail.jsx:1002-1039 (handleReplaceExercise, unawaited transferProgressionState + ProgramEnrollment.update — race still unconfirmed)
why: Re-ran a single-swap scratch repro: the Replace dialog input (in the fixed bottom sheet from src/components/ui/dialog.jsx) sat at top=600 with the sim keyboard top at 513, and the warning fired. Root cause is the iphone-sim layer, not the app: its reveal logic (iphone-sim/layer.js ~223-229) did window.scrollBy on the scrollable page behind the modal (scrollY 0->277) and then set pan~0, assuming document scroll moves the field; but the field is position:fixed, so in the sim it does not move. On real iOS with the keyboard up, the visual viewport scrolls within the enlarged layout viewport and fixed layers move with it, so WebKit's focus-reveal brings the field above the keyboard. Would not bet on this on Nolan's phone; the fix belongs in iphone-sim (pan by the fixed-field delta when the focused element has a fixed ancestor). The 4-swap progression_state race hypothesis remains unconfirmed (cannot-repro here). Side note: my run logged a pageerror "program_workouts?program_id=in.(...) due to access control checks" on /workout-detail - the r1-15 lead may be intermittent; worth a targeted case next round.
rootCause: harness: /home/nolan/projects/iphone-sim/layer.js:223-229 (scrollBy absorbs pan for fixed-position fields); app code src/components/ui/dialog.jsx:29 not at fault
fixHint: No app change. Harness: in showKeyboard, if el has a position:fixed ancestor, skip scrollBy and setPan(pan+want). If a real-device tunnel check ever shows occlusion, add a keyboard-inset padding-bottom (var(--keyboard-inset)) to DialogContent.
